beats.t: Black hands fell like rain. One, two, ten, a hundred. Black threads hung from every finger, all their ends pointing at one child.
Yeoni, get up! Move!
Yeoni did not rise. Sitting still, they merely lifted their head and watched the descending hands as though sightseeing.
So many hands.
Yeoni.
Yeongnyangi lunged. The black thread at his neck pulled taut and caught him in midair. His paw stopped just before Yeoni's nose. One handspan short.
Con artist, get up! The pig's getting eaten!
I'm getting up. My legs just aren't.
Yundal was binding his bloodied wrist with his shirt. The hole had passed his wrist and was crawling toward his elbow.
The first hand touched Yeoni's shoulder. It did not grab. It seeped in. Like ink spreading in water, blackness slowly diffused into gray fur.
Yes. Like that. Empty places are made to be filled.
Inside Yeoni, all was quiet. Neither cold nor hot. Where favorite things had rested, only labels remained. Skewers. Songs. Bread. One star.
All empty.
Yet in one corner, something remained. Not fortune. Something the ledger could not take. Something like a habit rooted in the body.
The touch of a wet lotus leaf. A rocking ferryboat. A golden ring tightening over black fur. And a low, brusque voice.
Now. Don't pull. Push. Make a gap for the paw to slip out.
Push.
Yeoni repeated it. The meaning was still unclear. But their forehead remembered first—the feel of pushing the tiger's shoulder that day.
Yeoni stood. The black hand seeping into their shoulder faltered, as though it had never expected the vessel to move.
Yeoni walked slowly between the hands. Not toward Yeongnyangi. Not toward the others. Toward the black tiger standing frozen with the ledger.
Don't come. Our business is finished.
Yes. But you look hurt.
What?
Yeoni's eyes still reflected nothing. Yet they rested precisely on one place. The tiger's right forepaw. The golden ring that tightened a notch with every grip of the ledger.
Black fur had rubbed away beneath the ring. Under it lay an old circular wound, a scar that had healed and been squeezed open again and again.
That was tight last time, too.
None of your business. Step back, unless you want to get hurt.
I don't even have the fortune to get hurt. You took it all.
The tiger caught its breath. Its face could find no reply.
Yeoni bent low. And, just as on that day, pushed the tiger's paw with their forehead. Not pulling the ring, but making a gap between ring and paw.
What are you...
The ring loosened one notch. It did not break. But for the first time since that day, the paw could move a little inside it.
If it hurts, say it hurts. Stop putting price tags on it.
The tiger's red eyes shook. It knew where it had heard those words. And that this child no longer remembered saying them.
Why? You have nothing left. Why push someone else?
I don't know. My body just tells me to.
Tiger. What are you doing? Hold the vessel still while I fill it.
Yes.
The tiger answered and raised a paw, as though to grab Yeoni. The black hands settled all at once, seemingly satisfied.
The paw did not seize Yeoni. It wrapped around their back, and the tiger covered them with its whole body. The black hands pierced the tiger's back instead.
Ghh.
What. Are you doing?
I don't know, either. It isn't in the ledger.
A mere collector. Have you forgotten whose hands hold your ring?
I haven't forgotten. That's why it hurts right now.
The cloak ripped. Holding Yeoni close, the tiger rolled. Cold water splashed wherever they rolled. When it touched the black hands, they shrank with a hiss.
You.
Don't look. I don't like myself right now, either.
Strength left the tiger's paw. The hands embedded in its back still writhed. The ring on its right forepaw tightened again, as if in punishment.
At that moment, the thread around Yeongnyangi's neck wavered. All Black Moon's hands had converged on the tiger. One strand slackened.
Yeongnyangi swung his rusted paw. Its gold was half faded, but enough to cut a single thread. The white cat landed.
Yeoni. Can you hear me?
Yes. I can. It sounds far away.
Black Moon called you a vessel. If you can hold things, you can push them out, too. Not everything inside you belongs to you.
Push.
Yes. Everyone, give this child your breath.
Breath? How do I give someone breath?!
Mr. Otter, what Mr. Cat did during the breathing practice. A hand on the back. Breathe together.
Yundal staggered up and placed his hand on Yeoni's back. The hand with the hole. But instead of sucking air in, it breathed out warm air.
Ah, whatever! Pig, take my fire. Ten skewers later, though!
Moka pressed his forehead into Yeoni's side. A small ember moved into their fur. This time, it did not go out.
Last, Yeongnyangi touched his forehead to Yeoni's. Between the scents of rust and iron came the scent of a very old spring.
Take my Metal, too. It's a borrowed slot. Use it however you like.
At last, Yeoni's vines moved. They received and wound around their friends' breaths, one strand at a time. Fire, wind, metal. The first thing to fill the empty vessel was not Black Moon.
And one more strand. From where the tiger lay, cold, damp breath drifted onto a vine's tip. It smelled of rain. The tiger did not look toward it.
Stop. That vessel is mine!
No. It's mine.
A light entered Yeoni's eyes. Very small. Not fortune. A light shining from borrowed breath.
Yeoni stretched their vines toward the sky. All the breath they held burst out at once. Fire upward, Metal forward, wind sideways, rain downward. Five streams of breath pushed the black disk up.
This tiny thing dares...
The black disk was driven back toward the fissure in the sky. Its rim caught in the gap and warped.
Don't pull. Push!
The disk was sucked through the fissure. Beyond lay an unfamiliar sky, with stars arranged in twelve rows.
Remember, vessel. There is more than one sky. And you will be empty again.
The gap closed. The last voice snapped off like a tail. The black hands scattered like sand, piled on the ground, and vanished.
The sun returned. The river began flowing again. Light like morning poured through the mist.
Yeoni sank onto the riverbank. Their body felt strangely heavy. The weight of something filling a once-empty place.

[ Hour Stem 庚 · Borrowed slot · Reconnected ]
The chart appeared before Yeoni. All eight slots were lit. Only the first character, 壬, remained frozen black.
The chart's light flowed into Yeoni's body. Pink fur scattered like petals. Hooves became fingers. Short legs lengthened.
When the light cleared, a twenty-three-year-old woman sat by the river. Wet hair clung to her shoulders. Yeoni looked down at their hands.
Fingers. Five of them.
Wait, am I back? Human? Oiiink—no, no oink comes out! I'm really human!
The pig was a human? Why didn't you tell me?!
I did! I told you from the moment we met!
Who believes what a pig says?!
You're an otter! I believed everything the otter said!
As I thought. Good thing I asked for your birth date and time. That chart was far too human for a pig.
Yeongnyangi looked at Yeoni once, then immediately turned toward the river. The tips of his white ears were red.
Are you hurt anywhere? A sudden change like that must have startled you.
Why ask while only looking at the river? I'm right here.
I know. It's just... I'm a little startled, too.
My lady, shall we celebrate your becoming human with another compatibility reading? Human to human this time.
Business is closed.
Then raindrops began falling through the sunshine. Rain in sunlight. Everyone looked up.
On a rock across the river stood the black tiger. Its cloak was torn to shreds. The ring on its right forepaw was tight again.
Hey. Thanks for earlier.
I can't write thank you in the ledger. There's no column for it.
Then don't write it. Just listen.
The tiger did not answer. For a brief but lingering moment, it looked at Yeoni's human face. Those were not eyes seeing a face for the first time.
The rain thickened. The black shape blurred within it. When the rain stopped, nobody remained on the rock. Only one red pawprint marked the wet stone.
